Good morning, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How can I help you today?

Hello, Rachel. It's Adrian Lim. I'm at my desk and have some privacy, so this is a convenient time to deal with my portfolio. My identity card number is S six zero five eight nine one two M. My date of birth is 31 March 1964.

Thank you, Adrian. Before we get into that, is there anything you would like me to note about how we keep in touch?

I prefer concise telephone updates. It's easier if you start with what needs my attention rather than take me through a long introduction. I'm also planning to spend more time away from work.

I can keep the administrative updates focused. Will your usual telephone remain the best way to reach you when you're away from the office?

Yes, use my usual telephone. If I don't answer, leave a request for me to call back, without details. I'm trying to give my staff more room to manage the business without referring everything to me.

I'll note that contact preference. You won't need to be at your desk for a telephone conversation, but please make sure you can speak privately when returning a call. We can turn to what you wanted to discuss today.

The holding I want to transact in is Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031. For the holding I already have, I'd like to— Let me start again: I want to sell part of my existing holding.

Your objective is to free up cash from your existing bond holding and reduce your exposure to corporate credit. I recommend selling part of your holding in Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 to release cash and reduce your corporate credit exposure. Using a limit order gives you control over the minimum sale price, although it may not execute.

There is something about the original funding that I should tell you. The original purchase was funded with undeclared cash receipts from my business that I routed through a relative's account to hide where they came from. I now want to liquidate the holding.

I also need to cover the investment disclosures during our discussion. For Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, deterioration in the issuer's creditworthiness could reduce its resale value, and a default could interrupt payments. Limited secondary-market liquidity could also delay your sale. You may lose some or all of the capital invested in this bond. Selling below your acquisition cost would crystallise a capital loss. Do you understand how the issuer's credit problems could affect the bond's value and payments, and how limited liquidity could delay your sale?

Yes, I understand those risks: the issuer's credit problems could lower the bond's value or interrupt payments, and finding a buyer could take time.

The transaction fee for this sale is 0.25%.

The transaction currency should be US dollars. The monetary amount for this transaction is 10,000. The quantity for the order is 700 units. Please use a limit order with a limit price of 14.29 American dollars.

Please confirm your final instruction: sell 700 units of Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, with a transaction amount of 10,000 in US dollars, using a limit order at a limit price of 14.29 American dollars. Is that the instruction you want me to place?

Yes, I confirm that final transaction instruction. Please place the order as you have just described.

Thank you, Adrian. That brings us to the end of the telephone discussion. I've noted your preference about messages and keeping our calls concise.

Thank you, Rachel. I'll keep an eye out for any messages and return your call when I can speak privately. Goodbye.

Goodbye, Adrian.
